learning_outcomes.text: Knows the friction processes in mechanical systems specific to road vehicles under various operating conditions.
Knows the importance of lubricants, rheological characteristics, and lubrication processes in the engine, gearbox, bearings, joints, etc.
Knows the wear processes in mechanical systems components of vehicles.
Knows methods for estimating vehicle reliability in relation to complex friction, wear, and lubrication processes.
Knows tribological safety criteria in the conception and design of automotive components.
Uses stands to observe and monitor friction, wear, and lubrication phenomena.
Interprets the influence of various factors on friction, wear, and lubrication processes.
Calculates friction forces and moments as well as power consumed by friction.
Calculates stress states in punctual, linear, or surface friction couples.
Calculates film thicknesses for various operating conditions and for various lubricants.
Recognizes various types of lubricants and their destination.
Recognizes various wear phenomena and their causes.
Knows tribological safety criteria and can apply them in vehicle design and operation.
Knows how to use software for monitoring tribological processes.

Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the work group, applies effective relationship and work techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents himself in his field of activity by adequately using effective methods and techniques for lifelong learning.
Develops professional projects in the field of automotive engineering.

syllabus_topics: Tribology, science of friction, wear, and lubrication processes
Mechanical interactions, friction couples, tribosystems
Elements of topography specific to real surfaces
Contact stresses at the level of mechanical interactions
Lubricants used in tribosystems
Hydrodynamic lubrication HD
Hydrodynamic lubrication applied in radial bearings
Elastohydrodynamic lubrication EHD
Elastohydrodynamic lubrication applied to gear rollers and bearings
Hydrostatic lubrication HS. Applications to axial bearings
Boundary and mixed lubrication
Wear in friction couples
Tribological safety criteria
Determination of contact pressure in friction couples of classes I and II
Determination of real pressure in friction couples
Experimental study of sliding friction. Stick-slip phenomenon
Experimental study of rolling friction using the "spin down" method
Determination of lubricant film in radial bearings operating in HD regime
Determination of lubricant film in gears and bearings
Determination of wear intensity in friction couples
teaching_methods: Demonstrations of relationships and calculation examples on the board
Brief recap at the beginning of each lecture
Determinations of roughness parameters using profilometer

assessment_methods.method: Systematic observation (individual/team assignments, case study report)
Laboratory activity (completion of sheets, laboratory colloquium)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on scores and weights of each activity. Grades range from 1 to 10. A minimum grade of 5 is required to pass and earn credits.
